rows.label: George W. Bush
rows.description: 43rd President of the United States (2001–2009)
rows.hook: led the nation's response to the September 11 terrorist attacks

rows.label: Barack Obama
rows.description: 44th President of the United States (2009–2017)
rows.hook: was the first Black person to hold the nation's highest office

rows.label: John F. Kennedy
rows.description: president of the United States from 1961 to 1963 (1917–1963)
rows.hook: was assassinated while riding in a motorcade through Dallas

rows.label: George Washington
rows.description: Founding Father and first U.S. president (1732–1799)
rows.hook: led the Continental Army to victory before becoming the country's first leader

rows.label: Franklin Delano Roosevelt
rows.description: president of the United States from 1933 to 1945 (1882–1945)
rows.hook: led the country through the Great Depression and most of a world war from a wheelchair

rows.label: Joe Biden
rows.description: 46th President of the United States (2021–2025)
rows.hook: became the oldest person ever elected to the nation's highest office

rows.label: Ronald Reagan
rows.description: president of the United States from 1981 to 1989 and actor (1911–2004)
rows.hook: was a Hollywood actor before turning to politics

rows.label: Dwight D. Eisenhower
rows.description: president of the United States from 1953 to 1961 (1890–1969)
rows.hook: commanded Allied forces in Europe during a world war before taking office

rows.label: Abraham Lincoln
rows.description: president of the United States from 1861 to 1865 (1809-1865)
rows.hook: led the country through a civil war and ended slavery before being assassinated

rows.label: Theodore Roosevelt
rows.description: 26th President of the United States from 1901 to 1909 (1858–1919)
rows.hook: led a famous cavalry charge up a hill in Cuba and later helped build a canal in Panama

rows.label: George H. W. Bush
rows.description: 41st President of the United States (1989–1993)
rows.hook: led an international coalition that pushed an invading army out of Kuwait

rows.label: Bill Clinton
rows.description: 42nd President of the United States (1993–2001)
rows.hook: presided over a stretch of strong economic growth and a federal budget surplus

rows.label: Richard Nixon
rows.description: president of the United States from 1969 to 1974 (1913–1994)
rows.hook: opened diplomatic relations with China after decades of isolation

rows.label: Jimmy Carter
rows.description: president of the United States from 1977 to 1981 (1924–2024)
rows.hook: won the Nobel Peace Prize for humanitarian work after leaving office

rows.label: Harry S. Truman
rows.description: president of the United States from 1945 to 1953; politician (1884–1972)
rows.hook: made the decision to use atomic bombs against Japan to end a world war

rows.label: Lyndon B. Johnson
rows.description: president of the United States from 1963 to 1969 (1908–1973)
rows.hook: signed landmark civil rights legislation into law

rows.label: Thomas Jefferson
rows.description: Founding Father, U.S. president from 1801 to 1809 (1743–1826)
rows.hook: wrote the Declaration of Independence

rows.label: James A. Garfield
rows.description: president of the United States in 1881
rows.hook: was shot by an assassin just months after taking office

rows.label: Ulysses S. Grant
rows.description: president of the United States from 1869 to 1877
rows.hook: commanded the winning army in the civil war before taking office

rows.label: Gerald Ford
rows.description: president of the United States from 1974 to 1977 (1913–2006)
rows.hook: pardoned his predecessor for any crimes committed while in office

rows.label: John Adams
rows.description: Founding Father, U.S. president from 1797 to 1801 (1735–1826)
rows.hook: served as the young nation's first vice president before becoming its second leader

rows.label: William McKinley
rows.description: president of the United States from 1897 to 1901 (1843-1901)
rows.hook: was assassinated by an anarchist while greeting the public at a world's fair

rows.label: Andrew Jackson
rows.description: president of the United States from 1829 to 1837
rows.hook: survived an assassination attempt and was known by a tough nickname involving hickory wood

rows.label: Woodrow Wilson
rows.description: 28th President of the United States (1913–1921)
rows.hook: led the country through a world war and pushed for a league of nations afterward

rows.label: Calvin Coolidge
rows.description: president of the United States from 1923 to 1929
rows.hook: earned a reputation for saying very little in public

rows.label: Herbert Hoover
rows.description: president of the United States from 1929 to 1933 (1874–1964)
rows.hook: led wartime relief efforts before overseeing the start of a severe economic depression

rows.label: Grover Cleveland
rows.description: 22nd & 24th President of the United States (1885–1889; 1893–1897)
rows.hook: is the only person to serve two non-consecutive terms in the nation's highest office

rows.label: Warren G. Harding
rows.description: president of the United States from 1921 to 1923
rows.hook: died in office partway through his term

rows.label: William Howard Taft
rows.description: 27th President of the United States from 1909 to 1913 (1857–1930)
rows.hook: later served as chief justice of the Supreme Court

rows.label: Chester A. Arthur
rows.description: president of the United States from 1881 to 1885
rows.hook: took office after his predecessor was assassinated

rows.label: John Quincy Adams
rows.description: President of the United States from 1825 to 1829
rows.hook: was the son of a former president and later served in the House after his own term

rows.label: Andrew Johnson
rows.description: President of the United States from 1865 to 1869
rows.hook: survived removal from office by a single vote after being impeached

rows.label: William Henry Harrison
rows.description: president of the United States in 1841 (1773-1841)
rows.hook: served the shortest term after falling ill weeks into his inauguration

rows.label: James Madison
rows.description: President of the United States from 1809 to 1817 (1751–1836)
rows.hook: is remembered as the primary author of the Constitution

rows.label: James Buchanan
rows.description: president of the United States from 1857 to 1861
rows.hook: led the country through the years just before the civil war began

rows.label: Martin Van Buren
rows.description: president of the United States from 1837 to 1841
rows.hook: was the first president born a citizen of the United States rather than a British subject

rows.label: Zachary Taylor
rows.description: president of the United States from 1849 to 1850
rows.hook: died of illness after only a brief time in office

rows.label: John Tyler
rows.description: president of the United States from 1841 to 1845
rows.hook: was the first vice president to take office after his predecessor died in it

rows.label: James K. Polk
rows.description: President of the United States from 1845 to 1849 (1795–1849)
rows.hook: expanded the country's territory all the way to the Pacific coast

rows.label: Franklin Pierce
rows.description: president of the United States from 1853 to 1857
rows.hook: was the only president known to have delivered his inaugural address entirely from memory, without notes

rows.label: Rutherford B. Hayes
rows.description: president of the United States from 1877 to 1881 (1822-1893)
rows.hook: won a disputed election that was settled by a special commission

rows.label: Benjamin Harrison
rows.description: President of the United States, 1889-1893 (1833–1901)
rows.hook: was the grandson of an earlier occupant of the nation's highest office

rows.label: Millard Fillmore
rows.description: president of the United States from 1850 to 1853
rows.hook: sent a naval expedition that forced open trade between Japan and the West

rows.label: James Monroe
rows.description: president of the United States from 1817 to 1825 (1758–1831)
rows.hook: issued a famous doctrine warning European powers against interfering in the Americas
